method: Full pinned SSE2 C read and Git/SHA256 verification; comparison against already-read SSE4.1 source, without double credit.
findings: SSE2 substitutes rotate16 halfword shuffles and rotate8 shifts for SSE4.1 byte shuffles; blend_epi16 emulates selected16-bit lanes using equality masks and and/or operations.
Seven-round single-block message schedule keeps same diagonalization convention as SSE4.1; implementation similarity is not an independent oracle.
compress_pre loads full64-byte block irrespective of logical block_len, requiring padded accessible storage from caller. In-place output32 bytes and XOF64 bytes use explicit unaligned16-byte stores.
Four-input vector path transposes lanes and applies start/end flags per first/last full block. One-to-three remaining inputs call single-input SSE2 compression. Zero input produces no writes.
Per-lane low-word addition/carry and outer counter updates mirror previously reviewed SSE4.1 arithmetic; no actual x86 counter-boundary execution established.
Prefetch offset256 and vector instruction selection require platform/runtime qualification. Reading C implementation does not credit separate Unix/Windows assembly variants or establish throughput.
limits: No x86 execution or speed measurement; ARM parity remains a separate bounded result.
